rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lām can mean in or within, as in the scales set up for the Day of Resurrection and wishing one had sent ahead for one’s life.
rows.anchor: ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the command to pray from the sun’s decline, lām can mean after.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى بعد نحو ﴿ أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس

rows.speaker: ابن أبان
rows.claim: Ibn Abān says the apparent sense of lām here is causal.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبان الظاهر أنها للتعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a verb of saying, lām can mean about: the unbelievers speak about the believers, rather than addressing them, since direct address would say you did not precede us.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى عن مع القول كقوله تعالى ﴿ وقال الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One alternative takes the lām in the unbelievers’ statement as causal.
rows.anchor: وقيل لام التعليل وقيل للتبليغ والتفت عن الخطاب إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another alternative takes the lām as conveying the statement to its recipients and explains the shift from direct address to third person.
rows.anchor: وقيل لام التعليل وقيل للتبليغ والتفت عن الخطاب إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik classifies the lām in speech addressed to another party, including these examples, as the lām that conveys speech to its recipient; others use the same label.
rows.anchor: فاللام للتبليغ كذلك قسمها ابن مالك كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the person denoted by the lām is absent from the utterance literally or in effect, the lām is causal, as in these examples.
rows.anchor: فإن عرف من غاب عن القول حقيقة أو حكما فللتعليل نحو

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik’s rule is that when lām attaches to the person addressed by the speaker, it makes the saying transitive to its recipient.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن مالك وغيره ضابطا في اللام المتعلقة بالقول وهو إن دخلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage raises the objection that, since the question arose only because of fighting in the sacred month, it should have asked about the fighting rather than the month.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل عن قتال في الشهر الحرام لأنهم لم يسالوا إلا من أجل القتال فيه فكان ذكره أولى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the question came after the fighting; repeating the explicit phrase sacred month clarifies the ruling on fighting that had occurred in it.
rows.anchor: وقيل لم يقع السؤال إلا بعد القتال فكان الاهتمام بالسؤال عن هذا الشهر هل ابيح فيه القتال واعاده بلفظ الظاهر

rows.speaker: صاحب الإيضاح
rows.claim: The Jews asked to confound the Prophet because spirit can denote the human spirit, Gabriel, another angel, a class of angels, the Qur’an, or Jesus; the general answer frustrates their trap.
rows.anchor: إن اليهود إنما سألوا تعجيزا وتغليظا إذا كان الروح يقال بالاشتراك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says they asked whether the spirit is created; saying it is from the Lord’s command answers that it is God’s act and creation.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنما سألوا عن الروح هل هي محدثة مخلوقة أم ليست كذلك فأجابهم بأنها من أمر الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view identifies the spirit as the Qur’an, which God revealed to the Prophet as evidence of his truth, beyond the work or capacity of creatures.
rows.anchor: وقيل أنهم سالوه عن الروح الذي هو في القرآن فقد سمى الله القرآن روحا في مواضع من الكتاب

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Murtaḍā transmits this Qur’an interpretation from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and supports it with the next verse: God could remove what He revealed, showing the Qur’an is from His command.
rows.anchor: وحكاه الشريف المرتضى في الغرر ( 2 ) عن الحسن البصري قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses expanded his answer about the object in his hand because he sensed that a great event involving the staff was coming and wanted to describe its ordinary uses first.
rows.anchor: ومثال الزيادة في الجواب قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions gathered the revealed Qur’an between two covers without addition or loss because it had been scattered among palm stalks, stones, and memorized by people who might die; they wrote what they heard from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: إثبات ظاهر أن الصحابة جمعوا بين الدفتين القرآن المنزل من غير زيادة ولا نقص والذى حملهم على جمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet directed the Qur’an’s arrangement; the Companions gathered it in one place rather than determining its order, and revelation order differs from recitation order.
rows.anchor: وهذا الترتيب كان منه صلى الله عليه وسلم بتوقيف لهم على ذلك وأن هذه الآية عقب تلك الآية فثبت أن سعى الصحابة فى جمعه فى موضع واحد لا فى ترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an was placed in its present order in the Preserved Tablet and sent all at once to the lowest heaven, then revealed gradually to the Prophet as needs arose; the Companion consensus secured preservation, removed disagreement, and unified the community.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن مكتوب فى اللوح المحفوظ على هذا الترتيب الذى هو فى مصاحفنا الآن أنزله الله جملة واحدة إلى سماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī says the leading Companions shared the public recitation, the Prophet’s twice-yearly review with Gabriel in his final year; Zayd witnessed that final review, taught it, and was therefore chosen by Abū Bakr and tasked by ʿUthmān.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمى كانت قراءة أبى بكر وعمر وعثمان وزيد بن ثابت والمهاجرين والأنصار واحدة

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris distinguishes two compilations: the Companions arranged the suras, while the Prophet, by instruction, arranged the verses within each sura.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين بن فارس فى المسائل الخمس جمع القرآن على ضربين أحدهما تأليف السور

rows.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators understand the challenge to bring ten suras as ranging from al-Baqara through Hūd, the tenth sura in that count; the author notes that Hūd is Meccan whereas several earlier named suras are Medinan and later.
rows.anchor: وذهب جماعة من المفسرين إلى أن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret tartīl as reading the Qur’an in its given order without advancing or delaying; reversing it is condemned, and an oath to read it in order refers to this order.
rows.anchor: أى اقرأه على هذا الترتيب من غير تقديم ولا تأخير وجاء النكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suras and verses were revealed in stages to meet people’s changing needs; abrogating and abrogated material could not descend together, and gradual revelation’s chief wisdom is stated in this verse.
rows.anchor: وإنما تفرقت سوره وآياته نزولا لحاجة الناس إليها حالة بعد حالة ولأن فيه الناسخ والمنسوخ

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr reports different early mushaf orders: some followed revelation chronology, ʿAlī began with Iqraʾ, Ibn Masʿūd with al-Fātiḥa then al-Baqara and al-Nisāʾ, and Ubayy with al-Fātiḥa then al-Nisāʾ and other suras.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل قد اختلف السلف فى ترتيب القرآن فمنهم من كتب فى المصحف السور على تاريخ نزولها

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: A proposed answer is that the Companions may have arranged the suras by their own judgment, while the Prophet placed the basmala at the beginning.
rows.anchor: فالجواب أنه يحتمل أن يكون ترتيب السور على ما هى عليه اليوم على وجه الاجتهاد من الصحابة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the Qur’an first descended whole to the lowest heaven, then over more than twenty years; Gabriel showed the Prophet each sura and verse’s placement, so the full arrangement comes from the Prophet and changing a sura’s place disrupts its order.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن الأنبارى أنزل الله القرآن كله إلى سماء الدنيا ثم فرق فى بضع وعشرين

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybī allows surah with or without hamza: with hamza he derives it from what remains in a vessel, making a sura a portion of the Qur’an; without hamza he relates it to the preceding sense.
rows.anchor: قال القتيبى السورة تهمز ولا تهمز فمن همزها جعلها من أسأرت أى أفضلت من السور

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some derive the word from a section of a building wall, with one level following another.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من شبهها بسور البناء أى القطعة منه أي منزلة بعد منزلة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others derive surah from a city wall because it encloses and gathers its verses, comparing it also to a bracelet that surrounds the arm; on this account the wāw is original.
rows.anchor: وقيل من سور المدينة لإحاطتها بآياتها واجتماعها كاجتماع البيوت بالسور

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another possible derivation is rank, since verses are ordered appropriately within each sura; this supports studying correspondences between verses.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون من السورة بمعنى المرتبة لأن الآيات مرتبة فى كل سورة ترتيبا مناسبا

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī connects surah with elevation of rank because it is God’s speech and contains lawful and forbidden matters, and also discusses derivation from a leap or rising.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جنى فى شرح منهوكة أبى نواس إنما سميت سورة لإرتفاع قدرها لأنها كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī cites tasawwarū al-miḥrāb as descending upon it from above, linking the name surah to elevation and to parts built one upon another.
rows.anchor: نزلوا عليه من علو فسميت القراءة به لتركب بعضها على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s plural is suwar with a short u, unlike the plural for a building wall, sūr with a short u in the plural’s second syllable.
rows.anchor: وجمع سورة القرآن سور بفتح الواو وجمع سورة البناء سور بسكونها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some disliked saying a particular sura’s name, but the sound view permits it; Ibn Masʿūd’s phrase about the station of the one given al-Baqara is an example.
rows.anchor: ثم كره بعضهم أن يقال سورة كذا والصحيح جوازه ومنه قول ابن مسعود هذا مقام الذى أنزلت عليه سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: الجعبرى
rows.claim: Al-Jaʿbarī defines a sura technically as Qur’an consisting of verses with an opening and a closing, with three verses as its minimum.
rows.anchor: فقال الجعبرى حد السورة قرآن يشتمل على آى ذوات فاتحة وخاتمة وأقلها ثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: الجعبرى
rows.claim: Dividing the Qur’an into suras makes each sura, and each bounded verse, a distinct art and a sign; the range from short to long suras shows length is not required for inimitability, since al-Kawthar’s three verses match al-Baqara in miraculous character.
rows.anchor: وفى تسوير السورة تحقيق لكون السورة بمجردها معجزة وآية من آيات الله تعالى وسورت السور طوالا وقصارا

rows.speaker: الجعبرى
rows.claim: Sura divisions help teach and memorize gradually: children celebrate finishing each short sura, reciters rest at its end, and each sura has an independent theme, such as Joseph’s story or the hypocrites in al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: ثم ظهرت لذلك حكمة فى التعليم وتدريج الأطفال من السور القصار إلى ما فوقها يسيرا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the expression about the head blazing with grayness, the head means the hair of the head.
rows.anchor: ﴿ واشتعل الرأس شيبا ﴾ 2 أي شعر الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer in the instruction not to be too loud or quiet means the recitation of the prayer.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ 3 أي بقراءة صلاتك ولا تخافت بقراءتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction means the piety of the one who believes in God, with an omitted possessive relation.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولكن البر من آمن بالله ﴾ 4 أي بر من آمن بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase when he came to it, it means he came to its side or the place where he was.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فلما أتاها نودي ﴾ 5 أي ناحيتها والجهة التي هو فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the question whether the idols hear you when you call them, the implied object is your invocation, as the verse saying they do not hear your call confirms.
rows.anchor: ﴿ هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون ﴾ 6 أي هل يسمعون دعاءكم بدليل الآية الآخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s malāʾ here means his people or household.
rows.anchor: ﴿ على خوف من فرعون وملئهم ﴾ 8 أي من آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled life and death mean a doubled punishment in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات ﴾ 9 أي ضعف عذابهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeness is of the preacher of the unbelievers as a caller to livestock, who hears only cries and calls.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومثل الذين كفروا كمثل الذي ينعق ﴾ 10 أي ومثل واعظ الذين كفروا كناعق الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wives of the Prophet are like their mothers, with an omitted word of comparison.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأزواجه أمهاتهم ﴾ 11 أي مثل أمهاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two explanations are given: you make your provision a matter of denial, or you make denial the thanks you give for provision.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون ﴾ 13 أي شكر رزقكم وقيل تجعلون التكذيب شكر رزقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means upon the tongues of Your messengers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وآتنا ما وعدتنا على رسلك ﴾ 13 أي على ألسنة رسلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Your trusts can mean the people to whom you entrust things, such as a depositor, borrower, agent, partner, or another person holding property in trust; alternatively no word is omitted because the verb can take two objects and leave one unexpressed.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ أماناتكم ﴾ 14 أي ذوي أماناتكم كالمودع والمعير والموكل والشريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ask the village means ask its people and the people of the caravan; alternatively al-qarya may itself mean its community, or the buildings, since the addressee is a prophet with a miracle.
rows.anchor: ﴿ واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها ﴾ 3 أي أهل القرية وأهل العير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be understood with an omitted noun: the rites of Hajj are in known months.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الحج أشهر معلومات ﴾ 4 ويجوز أن يقدر الحج حج أشهر معلومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming of your Lord means the coming of the Lord’s command.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وجاء ربك والملك ﴾ 5 أي أمر ربك

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says the calf is literal in the phrase, signaling such intense love that its image could not be erased from their hearts; the common explanation is love of the calf.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل بكفرهم ﴾ 6 أي حب العجل قال الراغب 7 إنه على بابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iram is a place name in the genitive but is diptote because it is a proper feminine name; its femininity is confirmed by the phrase ذات العماد.
rows.anchor: فإرم اسم لموضع وهو في موضع جر إلا أنه منع الصرف للعملية والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern faʿlān is more emphatic than faʿīl; al-Raḥmān is thus more emphatic than al-Raḥīm, with faʿlān marking fullness as in غضبان.
rows.anchor: أما فعلان فهو أبلغ من فعيل ومن ثم قيل الرحمن أبلغ من الرحيم وإن كانت صيغة فعيل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains a poet’s use of raḥmānan for a human as arising from unbelief and obstinacy.
rows.anchor: فهو من كفرهم وتعنتهم كذا أجاب به الزمخشري

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reject al-Zamakhsharī’s answer as insufficient: the poet used an indefinite or annexed form, whereas the debate concerns the definite name al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: ورده بعضهم بأن النعت لايدفع وقوع إطلاقهم

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik says the poet meant one who possesses mercy, not the proper name that became established by common usage.
rows.anchor: وأجاب ابن مالك بأن الشاعر أراد لازلت ذا رحمة ولم يرد بالاسم المستعمل بالغلبة

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says the Arabs knew the name al-Raḥmān but were ignorant of its attribute, as shown by their asking ما الرحمن rather than من الرحمن.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن العربي إنما جهلوا الصفة دون الموصوف ولذلك لم يقولوا ومن الرحمن

rows.speaker: البرزاباذاني
rows.claim: Al-Barzabādhānī says al-Raḥmān means the mighty, just king, not merely one characterized by mercy; the cited verses associate the name with majesty, power, protection, self-sufficiency, and universal sovereignty.
rows.anchor: وذكر البرزاباذاني أنهم غلطوا في تفسير الرحمن حيث جعلوه بمعنى المتصف بالرحمة قال وإنما معناه الملك العظيم العادل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes salāman the object of the saying verb, as in saying something true or sincere.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون منصوبا بالقول أي يذكرون قولا سلاما فيكون من قلت حقا وصدقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parse supplies an omitted verb such as we greeted with a greeting; the text quotes a full clause after qāla but retains only part of it.
rows.anchor: الثاني أن يكون منصوبا بفعل محذوف تقديره فقالوا سلمنا سلاما أي سلمنا تسليما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reply that their Lord sent down good, khayran can be governed by قالوا as in saying a true thing, or by an omitted verb meaning He sent down good.
rows.anchor: منصوب بقالوا كقولك فقلت حقا أو منصوب بفعل مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asāṭīr is nominative because the speakers did not consider the revelation to come from God and it is not a direct object like saying something true; only the nominative parse remains.
rows.anchor: فمرفوع لأنه لا يمكن نصبه على تقدير قالوا أساطير الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here duʿāʾ means naming, not calling out: the sense is name Him Allah or name Him al-Raḥmān, with the verb taking two objects.
rows.anchor: فإنه قد يظن أن الدعاء فيه بمعنى النداء فلا يقدر في الكلام حذف وليس كذلك

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh supplies bلى نجمعها before qādirīn, making it a circumstantial accusative, with the omitted verb indicated by the earlier statement about gathering the bones.
rows.anchor: قدره سيبويه ب بلى نجمعها قادرين فقادرين حال

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ instead supplies نحسب, guided by the following phrase أيحسب الإنسان.
rows.anchor: وقدره الفراء نحسب لدلالة ﴿ أيحسب الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers Sībawayh’s estimate because بلى answers the assertion that God will not gather the bones, not the question whether a human supposes it.
rows.anchor: وتقدير سيبويه أولى لأن بلى ليس جوابا ل يحسب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another proposed estimate is بلى نقدر قادرين.
rows.anchor: وقدره بعضهم بلى نقدر قادرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggestion that qādirīn is accusative simply because it stands in place of a verb is invalid; that is not a recognized cause of accusative case.
rows.anchor: وقيل منصوب لوقوعه موقع الفعل وهو باطل لأنه ليس من نواصب الاسم وقوعه موقع الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ellipsis can leave a substitute that signals what is omitted: in this verse, the estimated response is that there is no blame because the message has already been delivered.
rows.anchor: ليس الإبلاغ هو الجواب لتقدمه على قولهم فالتقدير فإن تولوا فلا ملام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāffah mā prevents إن and its sisters from governing accusative or nominative case, as in إنما الله إله واحد and كأنما يساقون إلى الموت.
rows.anchor: والكافة إما أن تكف عن عمل النصب والرفع وهي المتصلة بإن وأخواتها نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء, mā may instead be relative: the scholars are its predicate, with its referent implicit in يخشى; the text notes mā can refer to rational beings collectively.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون موصولة بمعنى الذي والعلماء خبر والعائد مستتر في يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a preposition, mā can prevent the preposition from governing the following noun; another analysis treats it as relative, meaning like that which they have as gods.
rows.anchor: وقيل بل موصولة أي كالذي هو لهم آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Non-kāffah mā occurs after a jussive particle, as in the construction أيًّا ما تدعوا.
rows.anchor: وغير الكافة تقع بعد الجازم نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Non-kāffah mā can also follow a genitive particle or a genitive noun, as in the cited examples.
rows.anchor: وبعد الخافض حرفا كان ﴿ فبما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is added after conditional particles, whether they govern the jussive or not, as in أينما تكونوا and حتى إذا ما جاؤوها.
rows.anchor: وتزاد بعد أداة الشرط جازمة كانت

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says mā between a noun and its dependent is an emphatic extra particle according to all Basran grammarians; Ibn Masʿūd’s reading omits it, while others analyze it as an indefinite adjective or apposition.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج ما حرف زائد للتوكيد عند جميع البصريين ويؤيده سقوطها في قراءة ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فقليلا ما يؤمنون, mā may reinforce the expression as in فبما رحمة, or convey minimization; on the latter reading, the sense is little by little.
rows.anchor: بأنها زائدة لمجرد تقوية الكلام نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra lā after the negation is explained by the verb istawā requiring two arguments; another view repeats lā to make explicit that neither good equals evil nor evil good.
rows.anchor: لأن استوى من الأفعال التي تطلب اسمين أي لا تليق بفاعل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā with رب can express perhaps, as in the example perhaps the unbelievers will wish.
rows.anchor: والثاني كقوله ربما رجل أكرمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā in the third category accompanies قَلَّ and طال, as in the examples قلما تقولين and طالما تشتكين.
rows.anchor: والثالث كقولك قلما تقولين وطالما تشتكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth use makes a word operative in a conditional construction when it would not govern by itself, as with إذا and حيث.
rows.anchor: والرابع المسلطة وهي التي تجعل اللفظ متسلطا بالعمل بعد إن لم يكن عاملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth use changes لو into the sense of هلا, as in لوما تأتينا.
rows.anchor: والخامس إن تكون مغيرة للحرف عن حاله كقوله في لو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final use is emphatic mā, which some call a particle of connection and others an extra; the author prefers connection because no Qur’anic particle is meaningless. It occurs medially or finally, between tightly linked elements, and never initially.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس في القرآن حرف إلا وله معنى

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh treats mā in إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ as extra; al-Fārisī instead allows an extra lām, reading the sense as كل نفس ما عليها حافظ.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه سيبويه في باب الحروف الخمسة قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh reads mā in وإن كل لما جميع as extra; al-Ṣaffār says a relative reading fails because mā would refer to individual rational beings, and Zarkashī says one should avoid calling it meaningless.
rows.anchor: ثم قال سيبويه وقال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about taking desire as a god, the usual order would put desire before its predicate; the second object is advanced for emphasis, as when one says I knew departing, Zayd.
rows.anchor: وأصل الكلام هواه إلهه كما تقول اتخذ الصنم معبودا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī and others propose fronting and postponement: the sense is that God revealed the book upright and made no crookedness in it.
rows.anchor: الآية أي أنزله قيما ولم يجعل له عوجا قاله جماعة منهم الواحدي

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects that reordered reading: the book is complete in itself before it completes others, so the verse’s stated order is rationally correct and the proposed reversal impossible.
rows.anchor: ورده فخر الدين في تفسيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls al-Rāzī’s objection a surprising misunderstanding: proponents discuss word order for syntax, not the order in which the meanings become true; and if qayyim means upholding others, no reversal is needed.
rows.anchor: وهذا فهم عجيب من الإمام لأن القائل بالتقديم والتأخير لا يقول بأن كونه غير ذي عوج متأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more apparent parse places the clause making no crookedness within the relative clause of الذي, where it has no independent syntactic position.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن الأظهر جعل هذه الجملة أعنى قوله

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: A further parse makes the clause a circumstantial accusative from the book, governed by أنزل; on this analysis, the order is fronted and postponed and the clause is parenthetic.
rows.anchor: ويجوز في الجملة المذكورة أن يكون موضعها النصب على أنها حال من الكتاب والعامل فيها أنزل قاله جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashī catalogs Qur’anic names including admonition, reminder, noble, exalted, wisdom, wise, guardian, blessed, and the rope of God.
rows.anchor: وسماه موعظة فقال ﴿ قد جاءتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His catalog continues with the straight path, qayyim, decisive word, great news, best discourse, revelation, spirit, inspiration, and the seven oft-repeated verses.
rows.anchor: وسماه الصراط المستقيم فقال ﴿ وأن هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining names include Arabic, connected speech, insight, clarification, knowledge, truth, guidance, wonder, reminder, the firmest bond, similitudes, and truthfulness; Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qur’an is uncreated.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس غير مخلوق وسماه قولا فقال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Commenting on the Qur’an being named Arabic, Ibn ʿAbbās says it is uncreated.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس غير مخلوق وسماه قولا فقال
